chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: His own compositions and 'Gin Mill Special'
summary: He recalls co-written tunes and how 'Tuxedo Junction' became the hit side.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, well.

I wanted to ask you before we got back to that something about your compositions and arrangements. I mean, if you would sort of summarize, you know, your compositions and arrangements for us before we got off, completely off the subject of arrangers in the band.

Well, I have to go back. I wish I had a list. But, well, along with Ace Harris, I did a lot of writing with some of the arrangers. You know, I co-wrote. And, I did 'Gin Mint Special'. In fact, with Sam Lowe, I wouldn't, I'd have to have a list cause some, a lot of them I can't remember. It's been a few times since I went over some of the big band stuff.

Oh, yeah. I forgot [Mitchelle] about that. I did that with Jimmy. I'm glad you can kind of push me along a little bit cause there's a lot of them I can't remember on account of the years of the big band.

Right. That's, that wasn't, that was supposed to be the number one side. "Tuxedo Junction" was supposed to be the second side. It was supposed to be the B side. "Gin Mill Special" was supposed to be the A side. Well, that's the way it started cause the people used to ask for that mostly until we recorded it. And then, while it was on the vendor, the people started turning the record over. And, that's how it started to moving.
